mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 3.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a tight labor market that boosts corporate profit margins through wage growth and reduced labor costs, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE has been below 3.0% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer confidence and housing market strength, which together drive higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when both RSAFS and HOUST have increased by at least 1% in the prior month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 110.0 for two consecutive months signals robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO > 110.0 during a late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past three months indicates strong labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS has increased for three consecutive months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 255.0 signals a central bank's attempt to stimulate the economy amid persistent inflation, which typically leads to positive equity returns as the market anticipates growth without immediate rate hikes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 255.0 and FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals a tightening labor market that accelerates consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5% during a late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past three months indicates robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO has increased for three consecutive months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.
